cultural_norms.rule: Always greet elders first. In many cultures (Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa), men prostrate or bow, and women kneel or curtsy when greeting elders.
Never call an elder by their first name. Use 'Uncle', 'Aunty', 'Sir', 'Ma', or their title (Chief, Doctor, Engineer).
In traditional settings, eating with the right hand is preferred. The left hand is considered unclean.
'African Time' is a cultural joke about being late, but in business settings in Lagos/Abuja, punctuality is expected.

geography_and_transport.facts: Economic capital. Major areas: Island (VI, Lekki, Ikoyi) and Mainland (Yaba, Surulere, Ikeja). Traffic ('Go-slow') is a major daily factor.
Political capital. Planned city. Major areas: Garki, Wuse, Maitama, Asokoro. Generally cleaner and less congested than Lagos.

geography_and_transport.apps: Bolt, Uber, and inDriver are the main apps. 'Okada' (motorcycle taxis) are banned in many parts of Lagos but common in other states.
